tasks.short: Advise construction professionals on fire prevention and code compliance

steps.what: Advise architects, builders and construction personnel on fire prevention and code interpretation

tasks.design: Retain contextual fire protection advice with the engineer using {DOCS} and {EMAIL}. Bookmarks and existing reference material support the discussion without establishing a separate retrieval or answer-writing baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on building use, design details and the applicable code context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing technical records and communication channels support consultation.
tasks.still_hard: Explain how requirements apply to a specific design or construction question.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise incomplete information and challenge unsafe assumptions.

reach.task: Clarify fire safety implications of design choices

evidence.claim: Context-specific fire protection advice retains full time; no repeated clerical preparation burden is established.

assumptions: The baseline is advice and interpretation rather than a separate document search process.
Question clarification and source checking remain in s1.
No new automation service or added maintenance is introduced.
unknowns: Advice formats and repeated preparation burden
research_questions: Is repeated source retrieval separable and measurable outside consultation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Interpretation and advice retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design fire detection, alarm and extinguishing systems

steps.what: Design fire detection equipment, alarm systems and fire extinguishing devices for the project

tasks.design: Retain fire protection design with the engineer using {OTHER}, existing engineering design software, and {DOCS}. Existing calculation and drawing functions remain in use without being counted as new automation.
tasks.previous_blocker: A workable protection design depends on hazards, coverage, interfaces and operating constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing engineering tools support design calculations and drawings.
tasks.still_hard: Choose an integrated design that meets project-specific protection objectives.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve design trade-offs and identify unsafe gaps.
tasks.altitude: Own the engineering basis of the fire protection design.

reach.task: Coordinate alarm interfaces and power requirements

evidence.claim: Fire protection design retains engineering judgement; existing design functions establish no new labour saving without a measured repeated subtask.

assumptions: OTHER denotes existing engineering design software.
The baseline is design and technical checking, without invented drawing transcription.
Later building-plan review is a separate task and receives no duplicate design-time credit.
No new service or added maintenance is proposed.
unknowns: Design tools and repetitive calculation burden
research_questions: Which repeatable design calculations are absent from current native tools and can be measured independently?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Engineering design remains; existing tools earn no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review building plans for fire code compliance

steps.what: Check building plans, model properties and applicable fire code rules before automated comparisons
outputs: checked model and bounded rule configuration

steps.what: Compare supported building model properties against the selected fire code rules
inputs: checked model and bounded rule configuration
outputs: traceable rule exceptions and uncovered checks

steps.what: Review rule exceptions and unsupported building plan requirements to determine compliance findings
inputs: traceable rule exceptions and uncovered checks

tasks.design: Configure bounded checks in {OTHER}, a BIM rule-checking application, with source requirements retained in {DOCS}. The engineer checks model completeness and all unsupported requirements; a clean rule run does not certify building compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated property comparisons consume review time when models and requirements are sufficiently structured.
tasks.enabler_now: BIM tools support rule-based checks for fire stopping and accessibility.
tasks.still_hard: Judge applicability, model completeness and requirements that cannot be represented as rules.
tasks.human_edge: Own the coverage and conclusions of the compliance review.
tasks.altitude: Use explicit checks without losing sight of unmodelled fire risks.

reach.task: Resolve missing model properties and revision mismatches

evidence.claim: Solibri performs rule-based BIM checks including fire stopping and accessibility; that supports bounded comparisons, not complete fire-code certification.
The proposed time allocation and savings are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: OTHER denotes a BIM rule-checking application; configure available rules before building a new checker.

Designers and the BIM coordinator produce element IDs, geometry, compartment identifiers, rated-property evidence and model revision; four added other-role hours cover missing property capture and source corrections.

In s1 the engineer validates those fields, selects applicable requirement versions, records explicit thresholds and documents unsupported checks; its 35 hours includes all focal capture and rule mapping.
Missing or unverified properties produce uncovered checks and manual review in s3, never an inferred rating or automatic compliance flag.
Eight added focal hours cover rule updates and regression testing; unstructured plans or existing automatic checks can reduce savings to zero.
research_questions: How much comparison time remains removable after model correction, rule maintenance and uncovered requirements?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 22. E1 range 0-12 allows incomplete models, unsupported rules and existing checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare reports on fire protection issues and review schedules

steps.what: Select fire protection findings, source code revisions and proposed review schedules for reports
Draft reports detailing selected fire prevention issues with source-linked facts and explicit gaps

loop.purpose: Turn selected evidence into a readable report draft
loop.input: Checked source packet and fixed report headings
loop.output: Draft sections with source links and unresolved gaps
loop.check: Engineer checks every claim, date, code reference and schedule against the packet and intended meaning
loop.stop: One correction pass; unsupported claims or missing sources return to manual drafting
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates place facts but cannot express varied issue narratives without prose work

steps.what: Review report conclusions, code references and schedules before handing the draft to its owner

tasks.design: Use native templates in {DOCS} to populate factual sections from {OPS_SYSTEM}, adding a bounded prose draft only where issue narratives vary. The engineer checks the draft; no external publication, code interpretation decision or schedule commitment is delegated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected technical evidence must be turned into coherent reports for different issues.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and bounded drafting can reuse a checked source packet.
tasks.still_hard: Explain the practical significance of issues without overstating code conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Own technical conclusions and distinguish proposals from commitments.
tasks.altitude: Reduce first-draft prose work while retaining technical review.

reach.task: Check readability and traceability of technical sections

evidence.claim: Bounded source-grounded drafting can assist varied report prose; the task-specific design and time effect are model knowledge.

assumptions: The engineer produces the packet in s1 with issue IDs, exact work descriptions, dates, source code versions, selected conclusions, proposed review dates and evidence links; its 35 hours includes capture and checking.
Code interpretation and review-date choices are human decisions made during s1; the assistant cannot invent revised requirements or due dates.
The 24 remaining hours in s2 include traceability checks and draft repair, with final technical review separately retained in s3.
Use templates alone for fixed sections before adding the bounded drafting loop.
Six extra focal hours cover prompt, source-access and regression upkeep; missing evidence returns to manual drafting.
research_questions: Does source-grounded drafting save time after packet capture, claim checks and technical review?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=84; gross 16 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 10. E1 range 0-5 allows extensive repairs and one-off reports; technical decisions remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use traceable model checks and report drafts while retaining fire protection design and interpretation.
reach: Resolve model data with BIM coordinators
Check report clarity with technical writers
role.ambitious_version: A fire protection engineer who reduces repeated comparisons and drafting while retaining responsibility for design, advice and compliance conclusions.
